adjudications.title: Sentence-count repair fabricates semantically empty completion text
adjudications.rationale: The active response reliability repair path still calls _pad_sentence_candidates and inserts generic sentences whose purpose is satisfying the requested count; it can also append missing reference tokens to the first sentence without proving semantic fit. Structural conformance can therefore be reported after substantive incompleteness.

adjudications.title: Fabricated shared history is detected but not blocked
adjudications.rationale: The fabricated-shared-history detector records reasons, but the current path intentionally remains delivery or repair advisory because grounding is not wired into a blocking decision. A reply can therefore reach the user after the detector established an unsupported shared-history assertion.

adjudications.title: Internal-leak checker exceptions are interpreted as no leak
adjudications.rationale: The checker returns an empty reason tuple on its recoverable exception path, and the consuming bridge treats an empty tuple as admission. This is a reachable fail-open for user-visible internal-process leakage, although it requires a checker failure and is therefore medium rather than high.

adjudications.title: Any screen text can support an unrelated quoted screen claim
adjudications.rationale: The active screen-evidence check establishes that a capture contains some text, but it does not bind the quoted or paraphrased claim to text in that capture. A valid capture receipt can consequently authorize unrelated screen content.

adjudications.title: Capability-denial repair ignores current runtime availability
adjudications.rationale: The self-claim verifier classifies durable capability denials from text patterns without consulting current service availability or the request's runtime state. A truthful transient statement such as inability to browse right now can be rewritten into a false durable capability assertion.

adjudications.title: Surface-delivery turn state is process-global
adjudications.rationale: The surface-delivery module keeps mutable turn state in process globals and is reached by the active route and event bridge. Concurrent requests can overwrite or consume each other's delivery state because no session, principal, or ContextVar custody encloses it.

adjudications.title: Child-task tool receipts are invisible to the parent turn
adjudications.rationale: Tool receipts are stored as an immutable tuple in a ContextVar and recording rebinds the variable. Child tasks inherit the old binding, so their later rebind is not visible to the parent that performs final disposition, contradicting the intended task-tree receipt custody.

adjudications.title: Session-scoped waiters accept untagged replies
adjudications.rationale: CP313 changed TaggedReply.is_for so a nonempty requested session requires exact session equality. The current focused regression test proves an untagged reply remains queued while the owned reply is delivered; the three CP313 waiter tests pass at current HEAD.

adjudications.title: Concurrent waiters can strand each other's deferred replies
adjudications.rationale: CP313 replaced competing shared-queue scans with exact (origin, session) waiter registries and direct dispatch. Concurrent waiters now receive only their owned replies, and the focused concurrency regression passes at current HEAD.

adjudications.title: Terminal watchdog can mistake the runtime server for a UI
adjudications.rationale: The terminal watchdog's process scan can match an Aura runtime command line as evidence of a visible terminal/UI process. This is boot-reachable and can suppress the launch or recovery action while no usable terminal surface exists.

adjudications.title: Timed-out terminal stdin readers survive and accumulate
adjudications.rationale: Terminal input uses a blocking readline in an executor. Timing out the awaiting coroutine does not cancel the underlying blocked thread, so repeated watchdog cycles can leave multiple readers waiting on the same stdin and later consume input nondeterministically.

adjudications.title: Terminal output pacing blocks the event loop
adjudications.rationale: The terminal output helper calls time.sleep from async execution paths. The sleep duration is bounded, but it synchronously stalls the runtime event loop and can contribute to user-visible latency and watchdog lag.

adjudications.title: Turn-arbitration check and record are not atomic
adjudications.rationale: The check/record API is non-atomic in isolation, but current production code has no caller of should_serve or record_served; only tests exercise that delivery API. The live suppression ledger uses different methods, so the claimed duplicate user delivery is not runtime-reachable through this code.

adjudications.title: Missing turn IDs share one suppression ledger
adjudications.rationale: Active suppression and recovery methods normalize absent turn IDs to the shared key 'unknown'. The obsolete should_serve path is not live, reducing severity, but callers that omit identity can still contaminate suppression or recovery state across unrelated turns.

adjudications.title: Unified transcript has no session boundary
adjudications.rationale: The finding was true at CP310, but the current working tree adds a normalized conversation_id to every transcript entry, scopes the HTTP request ContextVar to the actual chat session, and filters every read through entries_for_conversation. The new partition tests and grounded-recall suite pass (41 tests), so the former cross-session singleton view is no longer the current implementation.

adjudications.title: Exact arithmetic verification loses integer precision
adjudications.rationale: The deterministic arithmetic verifier converts integer and exponentiation results through float. Values above exact IEEE-754 integer range can be rounded and then incorrectly accepted or rejected, undermining a path explicitly used as exact correctness authority.

adjudications.title: Accessibility capability probe synchronously blocks chat
adjudications.rationale: The accessibility condition invokes a synchronous subprocess probe with a multi-second timeout from capability evaluation on the chat path. A slow or wedged system probe can therefore block the event loop and the foreground response before work begins.

adjudications.title: Internet availability depends only on public DNS port 53
adjudications.rationale: The precondition probe tests TCP connectivity to public DNS servers on port 53. Networks with working HTTPS through filtered DNS, VPN, proxy, or captive-portal arrangements can be classified offline, producing false capability denial; the effect is reliability rather than a security breach.

adjudications.title: A late retry answer can attach to the wrong message in a session
adjudications.rationale: Retry work is keyed by session while answer_pending resolves the newest unanswered record. Two pending messages in one session can therefore cause a late answer generated for the earlier prompt to be attached to the later prompt, a direct truthfulness and user-visible custody failure.

adjudications.title: Pending-message processing is not safe across processes
adjudications.rationale: The pending store's coordination lock is process-local and the claim/transition API does not expose a durable lease owner. A normal single-server deployment limits exposure, so severity is reduced, but multiple workers or recovery processes can still claim the same record.

adjudications.title: Late answers are deleted before delivery acknowledgement
adjudications.rationale: The active route consumes and removes a pending answer before downstream generation and transport are acknowledged. A crash, rejection, or disconnected client after consumption loses the only durable copy, so successfully recovered work may never reach the user.

adjudications.title: Historical degradations are described as current blockers
adjudications.rationale: Degradation records include timestamps, but preflight interpretation does not consistently apply age or recovery state before describing them as current. Old resolved failures can therefore trigger misleading user-facing explanations or unnecessary deferral.

adjudications.title: Single-word choices cannot resolve recorded options
adjudications.rationale: Option resolution requires at least two matching tokens, so common responses such as 'first', 'blue', or a one-word label cannot select a known choice. This is a general conversation reliability defect but has bounded impact and an explicit-rephrasing fallback.

adjudications.title: Any successful action receipt can support the wrong claimed object
adjudications.rationale: The helper has weak binding if called alone, but repository search finds no production caller of unverified_effect_claims; its callers are tests. The active chat effect path uses a separate verification pipeline, so this alleged runtime acceptance is not reachable through the identified function.

adjudications.title: Autonomous conversation loop bypasses the normal stack with a canned greeting
adjudications.rationale: AutonomousConversationLoop is not instantiated or registered by production boot; repository callers are tests. The canned greeting defect exists in dormant code but is not an actual current runtime path.

adjudications.title: Autonomous conversation loop fabricates idle background work
adjudications.rationale: The described text exists in AutonomousConversationLoop, but that service has no production construction or boot registration. It cannot currently emit the fabricated idle-work statement to a user.

adjudications.title: Any successful step marks a plan successful
adjudications.rationale: The weak plan-completion rule is confined to the uninstantiated AutonomousConversationLoop. No active runtime route constructs that loop, so the claimed user-visible false completion is not presently reachable.

adjudications.title: Reflector does not pair questions with their answers
adjudications.rationale: The reflector is registered as a provider but its only conversation caller is the inactive AutonomousConversationLoop. No current serving path uses this output to answer or remember a conversation, so the asserted runtime consequence is absent.

adjudications.title: Generated momentum text is processed as incoming speech
adjudications.rationale: ConversationalMomentumEngine is boot-reachable and sends model-generated text back through process_user_input. The non-user origin is preserved in history, refuting the stronger contamination claim, but the content still traverses intent classification and the incoming state-machine stack as a new utterance, permitting self-response and unintended state updates.

adjudications.title: Demo repository root resolves to core rather than the repository
adjudications.rationale: The active demo-support path derives its root from parents[1] of a core/conversation file, which resolves to the core directory rather than the repository root. Repository diagnostics and file checks can therefore inspect the wrong subtree and report false results.

adjudications.title: Demo fallback labels generated diagnostic text as user input
adjudications.rationale: When the demo diagnostic falls back, it routes generated summary text with origin='user'. This grants machine-authored content human-turn semantics in the active demo route and can affect authority, memory, cancellation, and presentation.

adjudications.title: AST structure summary is presented as a completed diagnostic
adjudications.rationale: The diagnostic only parses and summarizes source structure but its user-facing language says a background diagnostic or core function finished. The statement overclaims execution evidence, though it does not itself authorize an external effect.

adjudications.title: Effect-claim renderer trusts unauthenticated evidence fields
adjudications.rationale: The renderer alone is permissive, but the active chat route calls it only after _verified_desktop_task_result has required all requested receipts, ok status, effect_verified, and nonempty effect evidence. The inventory's arbitrary-ok-payload exploit cannot reach user-visible rendering through the current route.

adjudications.title: Conversation engine races two requests in the same conversation
adjudications.rationale: ConversationEngine has tests but no production instantiation or service registration. The voice bridge's optional lookup does not find a registered instance, so the claimed same-conversation runtime race is not currently reachable.

adjudications.title: Conversation engine hardcodes Bryan as the user
adjudications.rationale: The hardcoded identity exists in the unused ConversationEngine implementation, but no active boot or serving path constructs that engine. It is not evidence of current multi-user behavior.

adjudications.title: External-chat messages are dropped when no FIFO reader is attached
adjudications.rationale: External chat is boot-reachable. Its outbound message is removed before FIFO delivery, and ENXIO or ENOENT causes _write_pipe_message to return without durable retry or acknowledgement, losing a reply when the reader is temporarily absent.

adjudications.title: External-chat FIFO protocol cannot frame multiline messages
adjudications.rationale: The shell reader consumes one line while the writer accepts arbitrary text and appends a newline. Any multiline Aura response is split or truncated without a length prefix or escaping contract, making normal rich replies unreliable.

adjudications.title: External-chat IPC uses predictable shared temporary paths
adjudications.rationale: The service uses a predictable shared /tmp directory and sequential channel identifiers, tolerates preexisting FIFO paths, and does not repair or verify ownership and permissions of an existing directory. Another local process can precreate, read, replace, or inject channel data.

adjudications.title: External-chat manager returns a channel ID after launch failure
adjudications.rationale: The channel open method catches launch errors without raising, after which the manager retains the channel and returns its ID. The caller receives apparent success for a channel with no UI; the impact is bounded to this optional surface.

adjudications.title: Background child tasks can mutate the active failure ledger
adjudications.rationale: bind_failure_ledger places a mutable FailureLedger object in a ContextVar. Async child tasks inherit the same object reference and can append after being spawned during a bound foreground turn, so the parent's final failure explanation can contain unrelated background failures.

adjudications.title: Any successful receipt can support every grounded completion claim
adjudications.rationale: The active chat and voice grounded-claim guard reduces support to any receipt with ok=true, without binding receipt action, object, requested predicate, or effect evidence to each sentence. One unrelated success can therefore authorize a false completion claim.

adjudications.title: A historical successful intention can support a current claim
adjudications.rationale: The guard scans globally completed intentions and accepts an all-success user-lane intention without matching session, request, action, object, or time window. Old unrelated work can thus satisfy current claim support.

adjudications.title: Grounded recall reads a global transcript across sessions
adjudications.rationale: The current working tree replaces both direct _entries reads in grounded_recall with entries_for_conversation, whose identity comes from the request-scoped conversation ContextVar. Cross-session transcript and grounded-recall tests pass, so the CP310 bypass is no longer present in the reviewed tree.

adjudications.title: Unknown transcript origins fail open as human speech
adjudications.rationale: The human-origin classifier treats missing origin as eligible and returns true when classification import or evaluation fails. Generated or system text with incomplete provenance can consequently be remembered and quoted as something the person said.

adjudications.title: Own-prior-turn context remains stale across turns
adjudications.rationale: The value is a ContextVar set during the request that builds the own-statement grounding block. Normal ASGI requests run in distinct task contexts, and a set in one request task does not mutate the server parent context or a later request task. No active reused-task loop was identified that makes the claimed cross-turn leak reachable.

adjudications.title: Hierarchy compacts memory after persistence failure
adjudications.rationale: The hierarchy orchestrator is only constructed by the inactive ConversationEngine and has no independent production caller. The persistence/compaction ordering concern is valid dormant-code review feedback but is not a current runtime loss path.

adjudications.title: Hierarchy compaction drops tool outcomes
adjudications.rationale: The lossy compaction is confined to the hierarchy used by uninstantiated ConversationEngine. No active chat, voice, or memory path consumes this hierarchy, so the claimed current recall loss is not reachable.

adjudications.title: Memory system learns Aura's own reply as user facts
adjudications.rationale: EnhancedMemorySystem is only instantiated by the inactive ConversationEngine. Current persistence and memory routes use different implementations, so this extraction behavior does not presently learn from live replies.

adjudications.title: Memory extraction tasks are unbounded
adjudications.rationale: The unbounded extraction task creation belongs to EnhancedMemorySystem behind the uninstantiated ConversationEngine. No production call site reaches it, so it cannot currently accumulate live tasks.

adjudications.title: One counterfactual phrase exempts an entire mixed ontology clause
adjudications.rationale: The active ontology guard skips a whole clause if it contains any counterfactual marker. A mixed sentence can place an unsupported present-tense physical claim beside a hypothetical phrase and bypass scrutiny.

adjudications.title: One digital term exempts an entire physical claim
adjudications.rationale: The ontology check treats the presence of a digital-system term as sufficient to exempt the entire clause. Unsupported physical or embodied claims can be conjoined with a digital reference and escape the claim boundary.

adjudications.title: Conversation CID lacks a database uniqueness constraint
adjudications.rationale: Although the schema lacks a unique index, both record_turn and record_exchange enter BEGIN IMMEDIATE before checking and inserting the CID. SQLite serializes competing writers at that point, so the asserted cross-process select/insert race is prevented by the transaction contract.

adjudications.title: Global current session routes active turns into another conversation
adjudications.rationale: The fallback _current_session_id is an unsafe API default in principle, but the only production conversation writer found is the active HTTP route, which passes its explicit request session_id for each turn or exchange. No current concurrent surface omitting session identity was found, so the claimed live cross-routing is not established.

adjudications.title: Reply provenance is keyed only by a stale global content hash
adjudications.rationale: Reply provenance declarations are process-global and retrieved by normalized content hash without session, turn, principal, or expiry binding. Repeated identical text can inherit an older declaration and be admitted or rejected on stale evidence.

adjudications.title: Reply-stream close sentinel can be lost under backpressure
adjudications.rationale: Closing a reply stream suppresses QueueFull when enqueueing the terminal sentinel. The active voice drain can then wait until its long timeout even though production has finished, creating apparent hangs and clipped completion.

adjudications.title: Subject drift scoring ignores repeated emphasis
adjudications.rationale: The active subject-alignment gate reduces tokens to sets, so repetition and emphasis do not affect the score. Short answers with one repeated off-topic term can be misclassified, while strongly repeated requested subjects receive no additional weight.

adjudications.title: Any task verb can block an answer about Aura's own process
adjudications.rationale: The subject gate treats broad task verbs as evidence of an external-task request. Questions about Aura's own process that contain words such as build, run, or create can therefore reject a substantively aligned answer.

adjudications.title: Mood cancellation applies to the whole message
adjudications.rationale: A cancellation or defer phrase anywhere in a mixed request can classify the entire message as cancellation. The active router can discard independent requested actions or context in the same turn instead of resolving cancellation scope clause by clause.

repair_order.rationale: Establish mandatory session, principal, turn, and origin identity before repairing evidence or delivery consumers; otherwise later fixes still bind to ambiguous records.
Bind every claim to exact per-turn receipts, effects, objects, captures, and failure evidence; make child-task evidence collection explicit and close historical/global fail-open paths.
Give pending work an immutable message identity, durable claim lease, delivery acknowledgement, and a close protocol whose terminal frame cannot be dropped.
Replace the unauthenticated line-oriented FIFO contract with private authenticated framing, explicit launch acknowledgement, durable outbound custody, and reconnect semantics.
Make repair regenerate missing semantic predicates or report partial completion, make detector failure fail closed, and parse ontology/counterfactual scope at clause or proposition granularity.
Identify actual UI processes and windows, use one owned cancellable input reader, and remove blocking sleeps from async terminal output.
Move OS probes off the event loop, cache them with freshness and invalidation, and determine web reachability from the actual governed HTTP path rather than one DNS-port heuristic.
Use exact numeric types, freshness-aware status, typed autonomous ingress, phrase/clause scope, and weighted semantic alignment rather than token-count shortcuts.
Resolve the repository root from a canonical source, preserve machine origin on fallback text, and distinguish static inspection from executed diagnostics in user-facing claims.

focused_tests.purpose: Verify CP313 made the two tagged-reply findings stale.

working_tree_session_isolation_tests.purpose: Verify the in-flight conversation-session partition made the unified-transcript and grounded-recall findings stale.

notes: Current HEAD changes tagged_reply_queue.py after CP310; the reviewed working tree additionally changes engine.py, grounded_recall.py, and unified_transcript.py and adds session_scope.py. The engine change supplies an explicit conversation ID but does not register the otherwise dormant ConversationEngine.
The session-isolation changes were uncommitted concurrent work at adjudication time, so their exact reviewed content is pinned by adjudicated_against_working_tree_sha256.
Refuted dormant-code findings are excluded from repair_order; they should not be represented as current user-visible defects unless those services are wired in later.
No finding was classified duplicate because superficially related entries require distinct fixes or defend distinct active call sites.
